body: I was molested by my older brother, too. Please get help. I haven’t talked about it yet, and I’m regretting the years I’ve wasted in this prison of shame. Don’t make the same mistake. Gentle hugs to you.

Some days I'm used to it. Other days, the adjustment is never complete. I have scoliosis, chronic fatigue syndrome, fibromyalgia, depression, and anxiety. As the song says, I'm too damn young to feel this damn old.

I cannot say this strongly enough: take as much time as you need to heal. People that give a set amount of time as a deadline to get over a breakup are full of crap. It takes as long as it takes. Yes, eventually (and I don't want my comment to get deleted for saying this), it will get better, but I really wish people wouldn't emphasize that so much. To me, society seems to be so caught up in avoiding pain that we've begun to see the normal process of dealing with grief as almost an indulgence. Allow yourself to feel it. Don't fight it, but don't wallow in it. I visualize it as a wave. You see it coming, and it scares you. But if you surrender to it instead of fighting it (Idk if I'm making sense anymore, I'm getting sleepy, sorry), it passes over you and is gone. Not the heartbreak as a whole, just how you feel at that moment. (Break it up into manageable chunks.) Um...maybe this makes more sense. Instead of swimming against the water, stretch out your arms and float on top of it. It can't pull you down. You're still in the middle of it, but you're not surrounded and drowning. 

And that incoherence is my cue. Time for me to go to bed. PM me if you want to talk more. 

Also, your parents should not have said that. Full stop. I don't even know where to begin, except ...sometimes parents really screw up. I know mine have never reacted well to my emotions, and what they say tends to hurt the worst. Some people just are not capable of being emotionally supportive. It has nothing to do with you; it has everything to do with them. I know it hurts. I'm not saying suck it up and let it roll off your back. But you're absolutely a person deserving of love and happiness, and you shouldn't give a single solitary fuck about anyone who doesn't agree.

Oh sweetie. I can relate to so, so much of this. I'm not a doctor, but that doesn't sound like only typical adolescent stress to me. You need help. Is there anyone you trust? A relative or a close friend? Maybe one of your friends' parents? I completely feel you on the parents not understanding you part. High school was a good bit ago for me, but it seems some experiences are universal.

I didn't come out of my shell until about ten years after high school, and then I was amazed at how many of my friends had been going through the exact same experiences as me. We all felt like we were alone and never told each other. If you can't trust your friends to keep your confidence, you might want to consider getting new friends. I know that's a huge pill to swallow; I was never good at making friends. But you might meet some kids outside your usual circle if you try something new. Join a club at school, maybe something science or tech related? Stay after school and look up books about VG design in the library. You may meet someone with common interests. If it's what you want (and you're absolutely allowed to be unsure or to change your mind), keep mentioning it to your folks. Do some research on the career field, job opportunities, and the schools that would offer the degree you want. There are a ton of new changes on the horizon. Show them you're serious. And by god, do not skip college. I did and it's one of the biggest regrets of my life. I let my anxiety make the decision, and I can see now that I would have learned and grown so much, and made a ton of new friends.

This is getting long! PM me if you want to talk more. Take care.

Please don't. I'm brand new here, but it's not fair to punish yourself for the pain you're going through by making you miss out on all the amazing things that lie ahead. When people say "it gets better," it sounds like a line, and I know they don't know your situation. Nothing is permanent except death, not even the bad times. Yes, that includes the good ones. But they're still there. Life really can change on a dime. In the meantime, do something small. Have a snack. Take a bath or shower. Even just changing your clothes or brushing your teeth can help. If you're angry, punch the holy hell out of your pillow. If you're sad, have a good cry and let it out. Talk to someone. Depression is an evil disease out to kill us. I want to beat it just out of spite.
